rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at mid temperature to elute all 6 compounds if possible and map the overall elution window without risking truncation. This gives a first view of retention spread and whether early peaks are near unretained or late peaks are still in the hold.

All pairs are vastly over-resolved, so the next move is to cut time aggressively while keeping the elution window centered on the observed peaks. From injection 1 the peaks elute roughly between phi 0.18 and 0.68, so a narrower, shorter gradient should keep all compounds in-gradient and reveal how much compression is tolerable.

Since all pairs still have huge margin, push shorter and slightly stronger at the start to pull the first two peaks earlier while keeping the last compound within the gradient window. This tests whether we can get t_last to about 10 minutes without sacrificing full resolution.

We have reached the maximum score, so now probe for the shortest still-fully-resolved method by steepening further. The current worst pair still has large margin, and this test checks whether more compression can preserve all R>=1.5 while keeping the last peak under 10 minutes.

Resolution is still comfortably above threshold, so shorten the gradient again while keeping the same phi window to isolate the effect of slope. This should show whether the first pair is approaching the 1.5 limit and whether an even faster maximum-score method exists.

The current method still has margin on the limiting first pair, so test the minimum gradient time on the same window. This directly checks whether the fastest allowed method still keeps all adjacent pairs at or above the 1.5 resolution threshold.

At 2 minutes the first pair is right on the limit, so lower phi0 one step to give the earliest pair a bit more retention and spacing while keeping the minimum tG. This should preserve the very short run and recover a safer margin above R=1.5.

Now trim the high-organic end one step while keeping the successful 2-minute gradient, since the last peak still elutes well before the run ends and likely does not need phi1 as high as 0.65. This may slightly improve selectivity/compression balance without sacrificing speed, and tests whether the final compounds remain comfortably in-gradient.

Lower phi0 one more step while keeping phi1 at 0.60 to further strengthen the limiting first pair at the minimum gradient time. This tests whether a slightly wider low-organic window gives a more robust fully resolved 2-minute method without pushing the last peak past 10 minutes.

The 2-minute method is already at the score ceiling, so use remaining budget to test robustness and possible extra speed via temperature. Raising T may shorten the run further, and this run will show whether the critical first pair is temperature-sensitive enough to drop below the 1.5 threshold.

Higher temperature hurt the first pair, so counter it by lowering phi0 one step to increase early retention and restore spacing while keeping the faster 45 C condition. This directly tests whether temperature can still be exploited if the gradient starts slightly weaker.

Temperature clearly compresses the critical first pair at 2 minutes, so increase tG to 4 minutes at 45 C to see if slope can recover full resolution while keeping a very short run. This defines whether higher temperature is usable at all or whether 40 C is the practical optimum.

At 45 C and 4 minutes the method is fully resolved, so raise temperature one more step at the same gradient to test the thermal limit. This checks whether additional temperature can shorten the run further while keeping the first pair above the 1.5 cutoff.

The first pair is still just above threshold at 50 C, so test 55 C at the same 4-minute gradient to find the highest usable temperature. This brackets the thermal robustness of the fastest fully resolved method.

At 50 C the first pair is only barely acceptable, so lower phi0 one step to add margin while keeping the faster 50 C and 4-minute gradient. This probes whether the same short runtime can be made more robust to the limiting early pair.

With phi0 lowered, test whether 50 C can now support the minimum 2-minute gradient while keeping the critical first pair resolved. This directly checks if a hotter and faster maximum-score method exists beyond the 40 C optimum.

The first pair remains the sole limit, and lowering phi0 improved it at 50 C, so lower phi0 one more step at the successful 4-minute gradient to maximize robustness. This also checks whether the early pair can be made comfortably resolved without materially lengthening the still-short run.

Having strengthened the critical first pair at 4 minutes and 50 C, test whether that extra low-organic retention is enough to support the minimum 2-minute gradient. This is the key remaining chance to find a hotter, faster maximum-score method than the current 40 C 2-minute condition.

The 40 C, 2-minute methods are the practical optimum, so use remaining runs to probe robustness of the back end by raising phi1 one step from the successful 0.65 condition. This keeps the critical first pair similar while testing whether the last compound can be pulled even earlier without dropping resolution below threshold elsewhere.

At 40 C the 2-minute method works but the first pair is close to the threshold, so lower temperature one step to see whether cooler conditions improve selectivity enough to create a more robust ultra-fast method. This may slightly lengthen the run, but there is ample margin under the 10-minute limit.

Cooling to 35 C improved the critical first pair, so test the slightly stronger and faster-starting phi0=0.20 condition at the same 2-minute gradient. This determines whether the cooler temperature broadens the operating window enough to keep the shorter-retained version fully resolved.

At 35 C the first pair gained clear margin, so push phi0 back up to 0.25 at the minimum 2-minute gradient to see if the fastest practical window can be made even more front-loaded without losing full resolution. This tests the upper edge of the robust ultra-fast operating region.

The 35 C, 2-minute method remains robust even at phi0=0.25, so take one more step higher in phi0 to find the most front-loaded fully resolved condition. This may further minimize early retention while still keeping the first pair safely above the resolution threshold.

We have bracketed the upper phi0 limit at 35 C, so now test whether raising phi1 one step from the robust phi0=0.25 condition can shorten the last peak while preserving full resolution. This explores the fastest back-end elution compatible with the currently best ultra-fast window.

The last run gave a fully resolved 2-minute method with a faster last peak, so use the final injection to test one more increase in phi1 from that robust condition. This probes whether the back end can be shortened further while keeping the limiting first pair above R=1.5.
